items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: But I didn't know him personally at all. I didn't know Joe Oliver.

ctx.x: Him. Mm-hmm. How would Joe Oliver do it?

Well, Joe Oliver did too. It's like I'm telling you, I didn't know much about him. The only time I saw Joe, when I first went to Chicago, I went to a place to call the plantation. Uh-huh. And I went to the Yuddy Band and I went there and heard him. But I didn't know him personally at all. I didn't know Joe Oliver.
What about out in the country? Did they play trumpet pretty much the same as in the city? Did they use the same tricks?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: And I didn't ever see Joe Oliver until I went to Chicago.

ctx.x: You wouldn't know my band might go there.

No. I didn't never get to see him. I don't mean I wasn't old enough to see him, but I just never, I'll tell you the man I first seen when I was kind of getting on my feet with Trumpet, the first man I seen, I ain't gonna lie, it was Bunk Johnson. I seen him on my excursion pass our home recently, going to Homer, Louisiana, and I went on that excursion and I saw him play. First time. And I didn't ever see Joe Oliver until I went to Chicago.
That's a funny thing, you can live in the same town with people and never hear him.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: And the first time I seen him was when I went to Chicago.

ctx.x: Well, I believe he got something out of it from Joe Oliver. That's a fellow I never did know could do, Joe Oliver. And the first time I seen him was when I went to Chicago. I didn't never see him down here. First time I saw him. I went to Chicago to the plantation one night, the whole show went out and I went with him. And that's the first time I seen King Oliver.
Was there any of the guys playing like Freddie Caput down here?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: King Oliver was gone. Johnny Dots was gone. I met them in Chicago.

ctx.x: The district. Oh hell yeah man. You was. I was playing with a fellow and Ken Beard in the daytime. Cans of the women, you know, the whole hustle of them. 10 cents a can and every night I'd get up there and play the blues with the piano player. Now he, I forget his name, he died. He was a sickly fellow but he died. But I, nothing but blues all night. I'd sit up and play the blues all night. A fellow named Tootlum. Tootlum. Gravity and Gravy. All right let me ask you this. It's known that Jelly Roll played here in…
Which band was it that Keppert was in you were in?
